Estimate the cost of automating one workflow

Count manual exceptions, review time and recurring charges before comparing an agency’s implementation quote with the work it could save.

Worked example

Consider an illustrative order-entry queue with 400 requests a month at six minutes each. That is 40 hours of manual work. If 80 requests still need six minutes and the other 320 need one minute of review, the new workload is 13 hours and 20 minutes. The potential saving is 26 hours and 40 minutes before maintenance.

Worksheet
InputWhere to get it
Monthly volumeCount completed requests in the source system. Keep retries and duplicate events out of the count.
Time after automationTime both a routine review and a rejected request. Include the steps needed to correct bad data and resubmit.
Recurring spendAsk for platform fees, model or API usage, support hours and minimum commitments. Price the same monthly volume for every quote.
Break-even pointMultiply hours recovered by your loaded hourly rate. Subtract recurring spend, then divide the setup fee by the positive monthly benefit.

Check what happens in a difficult month

Repeat the calculation with twice as many exceptions. If the monthly benefit turns negative, the setup cost has no payback under that assumption. Run a short trial on the hardest requests and measure the exception rate before signing.
